newsitem.title: UKRAINE: IMF may decide big Ukraine credit in July - adviser.
newsitem.headline: IMF may decide big Ukraine credit in July - adviser.

text.p: President Leonid Kuchma's top economic adviser said on Friday the International Monetary Fund was ready to rule on a multi-billion-dollar loan in July if parliament passed this year's long-delayed budget quickly.

Valery Lytvytsky was speaking to reporters after Kuchma met the Fund's deputy managing director for the second time in two days as parliament debated this year's budget, whose approval is a key condition for the $2.5-$3 billion Extended Fund Facility loan.

"The president supported the EFF programme aiming at structural reforms, where Ukraine is still lagging behind. Fischer agreed with this and said the IMF would do its utmost to get the necessary decision adopted by the IMF board in July," Lytvytsky said.
He said there was concern over the budget process, adding: "But at the same time both sides think the circumstances are there to start the programme. Time is the main limiting factor."
Parliament has extended its summer session to mid-July to allow extra time for the budget to be passed and deputies are due to start considering it article by article from Tuesday.
"In July all the necessary decisions on the programme should be taken," Lytvytsky said.

Ukraine says it has fulfilled 27 out of 41 conditions to qualify for the EFF but the Fund says that apart from the budget, steps to deregulate the private sector, reform the tax system and to strengthen its banks must still be approved.
Lytvytsky said Ukraine would not swerve from the course of economic reform set by Kuchma in 1994.
